svg.aria-label: leakguard output on a deliberately leaky forecast: five findings

g.text: examples/leaky_forecast.py:9:18: LG004 `.bfill()` fills gaps with later values. On a
time series, this leaks the future. Use ffill() instead.
examples/leaky_forecast.py:10:18: LG002 `rolling(..., center=True)` uses values after
each row. On time series data, remove center=True.
examples/leaky_forecast.py:11:27: LG001 `.shift(-1)` moves later values into this row.
This is correct for a target, but it is a leak in a feature.
that `train_test_split` (line 16) later puts in the test set. Their statistics leak
into training. Split first and fit on the training rows only, or use a Pipeline.
examples/leaky_forecast.py:16:36: LG006 `train_test_split` (shuffle is True by default)
shuffles data that is ordered in time, so some training rows come after test rows.

text.tspan: exit code 1. Codes: 1 findings, 0 no known pattern (not proof), 2 not fully checked.
